conditions: unless a new architecture reliably tracking provenance is invented

statement.excerpt: Unless and until somebody can invent a new architecture that can reliably track provenance of generative text and/or generative images, infringement – often not at the request of the user — will continue.
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

from_speaker: often not at the request of the user
our_interpretation: The forecast begins on 2023-12-29 and has no stated deadline.
Provenance means tracing generated material to underlying sources, rather than identifying the generating model.
The antecedent is the continued absence of an invented architecture meeting that capability. The wording says invention, not merely commercial deployment.
“Often” requires evidence of a recurring unintended-output problem; one deliberately elicited example cannot establish its frequency.
Copyright infringement requires a legal basis. Recognizable character generation alone is evidence of risk, not an automatic legal finding.
criteria.support_condition: While the absence of a qualifying provenance architecture is established, dated evidence shows continuing infringement and recurring outputs that users did not request to copy.
criteria.contradiction_condition: While that antecedent remains established, compelling evidence shows infringement has been eliminated across the relevant systems without such an architecture.

evidence.explanation: The study documents a mechanism through which generic prompts produce recognizable characters. It supports the continued-risk component, but deliberately selected experimental prompts do not measure how often ordinary users unintentionally infringe.

evidence.publisher: Landgericht München I, official court press release
evidence.explanation: The court reported that the output-related infringement was not covered by a statutory exception. This supports continued infringement in a specific German case, but does not establish unintended-use frequency or the provenance antecedent.
This research describes unresolved provenance problems in code-generation tools. It does not establish that no qualifying text or image architecture had been invented anywhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence establishing the provenance condition for a dated period, together with legally grounded output records and repeated unintended-copying examples; alternatively, conclusive elimination without the proposed architecture.
